## The defect

Two test sites outside the live-DC tier are the same **fail-OPEN** class as bug
`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` / `f0fb-de7a-b315-4508`, under a different phrasing. Each spawns a REAL
child with `subprocess.run`, never asserts a returncode, and its ONLY assertion is that some
string is ABSENT from the captured output. A child killed by a signal writes nothing, so the
absent-string assertion is trivially satisfied and the test reports GREEN for a run that never
executed.

Proven mechanism (bug `0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e`, 4/4 deterministic): a child that SIGKILLs itself
yields `returncode == -9` with `stdout == stderr == ""`.

### Site 1 — `tests/unit/test_git_floor_gate_tree_skew.py:127`

`test_absent_floor_file_emits_no_workflow_error`. `_run_gate` (line ~54) is
`subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", gate_script], capture_output=True)` with no `check=True` and no
returncode assertion. The whole test body is three lines and its only assertion is:

    assert "::error::" not in (result.stdout + result.stderr)

A reaped or OOM-killed bash child gives empty streams, so the gate script never ran and the test
still passes. This is a **success/health oracle** — the dangerous direction.

### Site 2 — `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py:151`

`test_reconcile_is_routed_...` (the non-integration one). Real child via `_cli(...)`. No
returncode assertion anywhere in the test; the sole assertion is:

    assert "unknown subcommand 'reconcile'" not in (cp.stdout + cp.stderr).lower()

Empty output from a signal-killed child satisfies it, so a never-started CLI reads as "the
dispatcher routed correctly".

### Borderline (lower risk, worth a look)

`tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243` — `_run_redispatch` asserts
`completed.returncode != 0`, which a `-9` / `137` exit ALSO satisfies, so the returncode check
does not fully close the gap. It is a message-quality oracle on a deliberately-failing run, so
the residual risk is low, but `!= 0` is the wrong shape for the same reason.

## Why it was not fixed in scope

Filed rather than fixed because both files sit outside the file lane of
`0e1d-c698-c38d-4c3e` (the live-DC test files plus their shared helper) and were held by other
sessions at the time. They are also a different construct — an absent-string oracle over
`stdout + stderr`, not the `assert "Traceback" not in cp.stderr` shape — so folding them in
would have widened that change past what one review can carry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Neither site can pass on a signal-killed child: the returncode is asserted, not only the
      absence of a string in the captured output.
- [x] A RED test proves it for each site — the child forced to die on a signal (empty output)
      makes the assertion fail before the fix, and the failure names the signal after it.
- [x] `test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:243`'s `returncode != 0` is tightened or explicitly
      justified, since a signal kill satisfies `!= 0`.
- [x] Reuse `tests/_child_diag.py` (`child_failure_detail` / `assert_child_ran_clean`) rather
      than re-deriving the message, so every tier fails identically.
